derivation: Generated by `python tools/board_manifest.py` (this board's row, read through tools/import_board.py) from the vendor's own EAGLE 9.6.2 board file, element J1 (THING_PLUS). Pad centres are the coordinates the file states, in millimetres, with EAGLE's upward Y axis flipped once against a 22.86 x 58.42 mm outline taken from layer 20 (Dimension), plus a 1.0 mm margin. Pad names are the net each pad is on, from <signals>. Nothing here was measured off an image. Scaled at 8.0 px/mm.
assumption: Every `pin` is null: that field is the rcontrol pin index of a PICSimLab board implementation (webui/pinmap.py), and none exists for this board. `chip_pin` and `chip_index` are what tools/import_pindefs.py read out of the sources named in `pindefs`, and each pad's `chip_pin_from` says which; a pad whose `chip_pin` is null says why in `why_null`. webui/boards/esp32c6.py describes the ESP32-C6, and its table is keyed by the labels of XIAO-ESP32-C6-DIP, XIAO-ESP32-C6-SMD, which are not this board's; no level is read through it for any pad here. The pin view reads a pad's level at its own `chip_index` instead, so a pad with one answers for itself and a pad without one is reported as not modelled.

pindefs.derivation: Generated by tools/import_pindefs.py from the sources in `packages`, at those revisions; a board file's `sha256:` is the first twelve hex of the sha256 of its text, newlines as LF. The board-support package names a pin by a pad's label. The vendor's board file names one by copper: the chip pad the pad's net reaches, directly or through one resistor in series, read against the datasheet table its `pin_table` cites. A net on pads that table gives no GPIO says so in `why_null`; one on a pad it does not transcribe, or named for a GPIO it does not reach, is refused. Each resolved pad's `chip_pin_from` names the sources that named it; where two disagree the pad is null and `disputed_by` names them. `python tools/import_pindefs.py <board>` prints the path each trace took.

pin_table.cite: ESP32-C6-WROOM-1 & WROOM-1U Datasheet v1.4, pp. 10-11, 3.2 Pin Description and Table 3-1 Pin Definitions: No. against the GPIO its Function names

pads.label: V_USB
pads.why_null: no board-support package covering this board defines this label

pads.label: VREG_EN
pads.why_null: the enable of the board's regulator, not a pin of the ESP32-C6: SparkFun's Thing_Plus_ESP32_C6.sch puts the net VREG_EN on U2's `EN` (an RT9080-33GJ5, whose `OUT` is the 3.3V net) and R8, and on no pin of U1

pads.label: V_BATT
pads.why_null: no board-support package covering this board defines this label

pads.label: GND
pads.why_null: no GPIO: the vendor's board file traces GND -> U1 2 pads = GND; pad 29 = EPAD (ESP32-C6-WROOM-1 & WROOM-1U Datasheet v1.4, pp. 10-11, 3.2 Pin Description and Table 3-1 Pin Definitions: No. against the GPIO its Function names)

pads.label: LED_DO
pads.why_null: no ESP32-C6 pin is on this net: SparkFun's Thing_Plus_ESP32_C6.sch puts LED_DO on this pad and pin 1 of the jumper RGB (JUMPER-SMT_2_NO), whose pin 2 is the `DO` of the WS2812 D5

pads.label: 3.3V
pads.why_null: no GPIO: the vendor's board file traces 3.3V -> U1 pad 2 = 3V3 (ESP32-C6-WROOM-1 & WROOM-1U Datasheet v1.4, pp. 10-11, 3.2 Pin Description and Table 3-1 Pin Definitions: No. against the GPIO its Function names)

pads.label: ESP_EN
pads.why_null: the enable pin of the ESP32-C6-WROOM-1 module, not a GPIO: SparkFun's Thing_Plus_ESP32_C6.sch puts the net ESP_EN on U1's `EN`, the RESET switch, R11 and C5, and U1's GPIOs are its `IOn` pins
